section.title: Introduction

epigraph.simpara: あなたがたは一体、終わりを求めるために、はじめを見出したのか。なぜなら、はじめのあるところに、そこに終わりがあるであろうから。

section.simpara: This document sets out our vision for the project: what it is, why it matters, and how we intend to make it succeed.

section.title: Purpose

epigraph.simpara: 不忘初心，而必果本願也。

section.simpara: Formal methods and model-based approaches to software development gained industrial traction in the 1960s–1980s through close collaboration between academia and industries operating under extreme safety and reliability demands — the earliest being defence, aerospace, and nuclear power. Their use broadened during the 1990s–2000s to other life-critical (railways, automotive, medical devices) and high-stakes domains (hardware design, finance). They are now gradually entering mainstream software engineering, finding applications in cloud computing, cybersecurity, and blockchain.
Papillon Journey seizes this momentum and tackles three persistent barriers to broader adoption:

listitem.simpara: Limited exposure. The historical confinement of these approaches to high-assurance niches has reinforced the misconception that they are irrelevant to the daily concerns of most software professionals. Demonstrating their power through large-scale, open-source initiatives in web, mobile, and game development will help dispel this view. That is why Papillon Journey will be cross-platform — playable directly in a web browser or via native applications on smartphones, tablets, and PCs, including handheld gaming PCs.

Fragmented tooling. Companies favour tools that integrate smoothly into existing workflows. Those supporting formal methods — narrowly specialised and rarely interoperable — often fail to do so. Chrysal Studio, the research subproject of Papillon Journey, will explore and prototype an integrated engineering environment to change that. We will start building with the patchwork of disjointed tools available today, transitioning progressively to Chrysal Studio, until it can fully sustain both itself and the game.

Inverted pedagogy. Children learn to add and multiply long before they ever hear of ring theory — and only if they choose to. Yet formal modelling is typically taught the other way around: heavy on theory, light on practice, and illustrated with simplistic toy examples that bear little resemblance to the challenges encountered in industry. Fusing the experience of a JRPG (for example, Final Fantasy) with that of a training platform (such as Coursera) without breaking immersion is no small feat. One thing is certain, though: learners will spend most of their time practising. The very nature of JRPGs will steer us away from the pitfall of inverted pedagogy.

section.simpara: For Papillon Journey to be a living example of what it teaches, it must be libre: open for study, contribution, and adaptation. We require only that derivatives remain libre and clearly distinguishable from the official project by their own branding and trademarks.
Formal engineering deserves wider visibility through a transparent, participatory, and engaging real-world use case accessible across various devices.

section.title: Stakeholders and value propositions

epigraph.simpara: 天は人の上に人を造らず人の下に人を造らずといへり。

section.simpara: Value propositions evolve alongside the people they serve. As their goals, challenges, and expectations shift, some facets are reinvented and others phased out. Even so, certain core needs persist, and these are what keep a project relevant over time. Below, we outline those that matter most to our stakeholders and map them to value propositions. For a deeper dive, see γ.

section.title: Video game players
section.simpara:
Training is future-oriented: the time and effort invested in it aim to unlock later payoffs — a job, promotion, career pivot, or proficiency. There is no such thing as training for the sake of it. The appeal of gaming, on the other hand, is precisely a break from that logic. Players expect games to provide a brief window in their day through which they can throw out all future concerns and fully enjoy the present moment. An experience that fails to honour this misses the whole point.
This is why Papillon Journey will be, above all, fun.

It will be a play-anywhere-anytime game by design. The web version will render 2D isometric visuals with vector-based, hand-drawn art that looks great and performs beautifully on everything from smartphones to desktops. Where hardware permits, native editions on Windows, Linux, Android, iOS/iPadOS, and HarmonyOS will elevate the experience with enhanced 2.5D graphics, richer lighting, and added depth. Progress will synchronise across all platforms, so players can switch between devices.

Using in-game systems such as courier services or trading posts, players will be able to share resources, discoveries, and hard-won strategies whenever it suits them, without needing to be online at the same time.
Certain locations and NPCs will also offer mini-games in which they can compete live. These multiplayer features will feel like part of the world rather than something bolted on.

As the player base expands, Papillon Journey will pursue partnerships with renowned game franchises to create crossover content. Such scope-limited collaborations will reconnect players with characters and stories they already love while they learn formal engineering. For partner studios, this will be a distinctive opportunity to associate their franchises with education, skill-building, and positive social impact.

section.title: Software engineering learners
section.simpara: The initial training of a software engineer reaches a satisfying end once they have the skills to turn software ideas into working, maintainable systems. Teamwork is one of them, as most systems are built through collaborative effort. Continuing education then becomes a pursuit of mastery and specialisation.
Papillon Journey will support both stages of the learners’ journey in two mutually reinforcing ways:

listitem.simpara: The fundamentals will be woven into the gameplay, so learners build skills through playful practice of product and project management, UX design, specification, development, verification, and validation. As they advance the story, the levelling up of their characters will mirror their own progress, with the climactic endgame putting their skills to the ultimate test.

For learners eager to apply lessons learnt in-game to real-world scenarios, the project’s libre codebase will serve as an expansive playground for deeper mastery. The comprehensive and high-quality documentation will empower them to study, contribute to, and adapt it with confidence. Dedicated community channels will foster support, collaboration, and knowledge sharing, ensuring no one navigates this journey alone.

section.simpara: We never truly know something until we teach it to someone else. Papillon Journey will provide a modding framework that enables players to upskill one another. It will facilitate the creation of custom downloadable content (DLC) that transforms visuals, reshapes the soundscape, alters game mechanics, introduces new quests, tells new stories, and covers additional training topics. By officially embracing modding, we will motivate learners to dive into the source code and practise formal engineering in earnest.

Mods featured in-game will be selected through a transparent, fair, and community-driven peer-review process in which learners actively participate. To maintain a clear legal boundary, they will be indexed from third-party repositories rather than hosted on the project’s infrastructure. The process will filter out insecure or IP-infringing content, protecting the Papillon Journey trademark from association with harmful or unauthorised material. Any that erroneously slipped through will be de-indexed upon report, and every mod update will have to undergo re-evaluation before being re-indexed. Beyond risk mitigation, this collaborative effort will sharpen learners’ awareness of the cross-cutting concerns of security, legal compliance, and quality assurance.

Spending time with the modding framework may awaken in some learners a passion for game design, and they may aspire to turn it into a profession. For them, Papillon Journey will offer premium guides and tutorials co-authored with experienced studios. Delivered across multiple media, these materials will draw on concrete examples and exercises straight from the modding framework, giving learners experience in crafting games on par with professional productions. For partner studios, this will be a distinctive opportunity to invest in people who are more than fans — who look to them as inspiration for a career of their own.

section.title: Software engineering educators
section.simpara: Software engineering is a vast discipline whose frontier keeps expanding — rapidly. Without guidance, newcomers can easily feel lost or remain trapped at the surface, chasing one trend after another while missing both the broader picture and the deeper foundations. The educator’s role is to help them navigate the field, meeting them where they are and guiding them towards where they want or need to go.

Effective navigation relies on reference points: at sea, a lighthouse; ashore, a landmark. For educators, the equivalent is a canonical work — a book, a research paper, or a project — that learners can steer by. Formal engineering does not lack reference texts; what is missing is an industrial-scale project designed to be taught from, so educators no longer have to rely on toy examples alone.

Papillon Journey will be that real-world project. Its engineering lifecycle will be anchored in industry standards — starting with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 and 12207 — while its documentation will be deliberately written as training material for classrooms and self-study.

Teaching is never one-size-fits-all. Not every learner thrives under lectures and routine homework. Play, by contrast, has near-universal appeal and offers a formidable counterweight to the sense of obligation intrinsic to every curriculum. By integrating the game into their programmes, educators will be able to sustain learners’ interest and re-engage those struggling with traditional teaching formats.

Educators at partner organisations will shape the play they bring into their classrooms by co-creating signature educational adventures. Their development will follow a dedicated partnership process, giving partners an official presence in the game through a route more prestigious than community mods. This will also offer partners a valuable way to showcase their expertise and the distinctive character of their programmes to a global audience of players and prospective learners, who may not encounter them through conventional outreach.

section.title: Software engineering practitioners
section.simpara: At its core, engineering is the negotiation, establishment, and preservation of the integrity of a system, and the continual renewal of that work to keep it fit for its evolving sociotechnical context. Integrity, here, should be understood broadly as the system ‘doing the right thing’; stakeholders do not usually agree at first on what that means. This is why integrity must be negotiated. Take a bridge proposed to relieve congestion on an older one: drivers may want a wide, modern crossing, while local residents may press for a design that does not disrupt the landscape and echoes the proportions and style of the existing bridge. Engineers mediate between such competing expectations, reconciling them with what is feasible within the constraints of schedule, funding, workforce, law, social norms, and the current state of knowledge and technology.

In software engineering, the integrity at stake is chiefly that of the software’s behaviour within the larger system it belongs to, and of the data that flows through it. The practitioners involved — across design, development, verification, and operations, to name a few — are collectively accountable to stakeholders for stewarding that integrity, whatever this requires in context.

section.title: Lifecycle
section.simpara: The project lifecycle is defined by outcomes rather than fixed timing. Its pace will depend on community building, community support, and the evidence gathered at each gate.

listitem.simpara: Éclosion. The project hatches publicly: initial vision, first prototypes, public devlogs, reproducible development and test setup for contributors, and early community.

Chenille. The project grows by feeding on experiments: gameplay, story, tools, pipelines, and feedback. It starts seeking financial community support and sowing the seeds for partnerships. A polished vertical slice and a mature Chrysal Studio form the maturity gate at the end of this phase.
Métamorphose. Full production begins: the project transforms from validated slice into the complete game, using Chrysal Studio only, while integrating and developing it as necessary.

Renaissance. The game becomes ready for public operation through rented infrastructure, deployment rehearsal, launch testing, operational hardening, and the partnerships needed to sustain it — including studio-co-authored game design materials once the modding framework is mature enough to support them.
Envol. The project goes live: promotion, community growth, maintenance, partnerships, expansions, and feedback loops.

section.title: Key success indicators

row.entry: Papillon Journey’s audience is growing: it resonates with players and attracts new ones consistently.
Papillon Journey has broken out of the software-engineering niche: its entertainment-first design succeeds on its own merits, regardless of its educational dimension.
Cross-platform play matters: a meaningful share of players switch screens, playing a significant portion of their playthrough on a secondary device.
Players keep playing beyond the initial novelty: the gameplay loop delivers lasting value.
Players reach the credit roll: the narrative and gameplay sustain interest from start to finish.
Players like the game: thumbs up outnumber thumbs down, and written reviews are positive.
Players are happy with the game: it nets a good score on a player satisfaction survey — calibrated to capture more nuance than a binary vote could.

As a player drawn to the genuine breaks from daily concerns video games offer, I would not say no to play sessions that also gave me valuable real-world skills. But, please, do not sacrifice fun for instruction. I want gameplay that puts entertainment first and lets me fully enjoy the present moment.
Share of non-engineer players: players have fun and gain skills. The two are blended well, and neither is sacrificed for the other.
Player retention rate: players enjoy the moment and keep coming back for more.
Player completion rate: storylines remain entertaining throughout, and players want to see how they all tie together.
Player approval rate: players say they are having a good time and leave more positive votes than negative ones.
Player satisfaction score: the majority of players report their play sessions as genuine breaks and rate the game above average.

As a player, I sometimes buy multiple versions of my favourite games for my home setup, handhelds, and mobile devices, or turn to cloud gaming when the hardware at hand lacks the power to run them. That flexibility is great, but starting my playthrough over is not. I want a game playable on any screen, with progress that follows me, so that I can always pick up exactly where I left off.
Player reach: the game meets players on the devices they already own and does not ask them to change their desktop, handheld, or mobile habits.
Share of cross-platform players: many players pick up their playthrough on a different device.
Player retention rate: players can continue playing exactly where they left off, whenever and wherever they are.
Player completion rate: players progress the same playthrough from start to finish, whatever the screen.

As a player, I like to feel I am not alone exploring the game world and uncovering its story. But in a JRPG, I do not want other players intruding on my playthrough. Unless I choose otherwise, I prefer our interactions to remain indirect and asynchronous — through in-game resource-sharing systems like courier services and trading posts — so that our journeys gently influence one another.

As a player, I enjoy competing live against other people. But player-versus-player is not a core JRPG tradition. I want specific locations and NPCs to offer competitive mini-games — where PvP feels right at home — so that I can enjoy the thrill of competing when I choose to.

As a player, saying goodbye to the characters who left an impact on me is always a sad moment. I welcome the chance to meet them again in another game, but only when it is done in a meaningful and respectful way, and with the studio that created them involved. I want official crossover adventures, so that I can trust the new stories I experience honour the vision of the original creators.
Hands-on mastery through the source code
Navigating cross-cutting concerns through mod governance

A real-world formal engineering project built for teaching
A formal specification language for the agentic era
A living use case to apply and demonstrate research in context
A unified engineering environment to host research-grade integrations

section.simpara: The same indicators are observed through different metrics as the project matures. The thresholds below are initial calibration targets: they make success visible at each phase and should be revised as real evidence accumulates.
